--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.layout_planar()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Place the nodes of a planar graph so that no edges cross. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.layout_planar()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Place the nodes of a planar graph so that no edges cross. title: >- [Graph.layout_planar()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Place the nodes of a planar graph so that no edges cross. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Place the nodes of a planar graph so that no edges cross. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6593-L6720){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.layout_planar( refine=True, scale=1.0, center=(0.0, 0.0), attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Planar layout](../assets/graphs/layout-planar.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, the octahedron graph (six nodes, each joined to four others) scattered at random, with several edges crossing. On the right, layout_planar() draws it with no crossings: a large outer triangle of nodes 1, 2 and 4 with the other three nodes inside it." width="100%"} Finds a planar embedding (see `check_planarity()`), adds edges to make it 2-connected and to triangulate every face but the largest, which becomes the outer face, and then places the nodes one at a time in a canonical order with the shift method of Chrobak and Payne. Every node lands on an integer grid point, `x` from `0` to `2n - 4` and `y` from `0` to `n - 2`, and the edges drawn as straight lines never cross. This ports NetworkX's `planar_layout()`, but that drawing crowds the nodes: the triangulation pulls them into a broad triangle, and nodes deep inside it can nearly touch. So with `refine=True` (default), a force-directed pass then spreads them out, as in `layout_spring()`: nodes repel each other and the edges near them, and edges pull their ends together. Any move that would make two edges cross, or bring a node onto an edge, is cut short, so the drawing stays crossing-free. The result is centered and scaled so the largest coordinate is `scale=`. A planar graph has many embeddings and this one need not be the one NetworkX finds, so even with `refine=False` the positions can differ from NetworkX's while being just as crossing-free. The refinement keeps every node inside its face, so a node in a small face stays cramped, and the drawing suits checking or showing that a graph is planar more than reading it. For a readable picture, a force-directed layout such as `layout_spring()` often draws a planar graph without crossings too. The refinement runs 300 rounds, each costing `O((n + m)^2)` for `n` nodes and `m` edges, with fewer rounds on larger graphs so that it stays within about a second; from a few thousand nodes it is skipped. Edge direction, self-loops and parallel edges are ignored. Graphs with fewer than four nodes use fixed points of a triangle, `(0, 0)`, `(2, 0)` and `(1, 1)`, in node ID order, and separate components are joined before triangulating, so they are laid out together. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [refine]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), spread the nodes out without letting any edges cross. If `False`, keep the integer grid drawing of Chrobak and Payne, as NetworkX does. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest coordinate after rescaling. `None` keeps the raw coordinates, on the integer grid when `refine=False` (`center=` is then ignored). Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the layout, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in. If `None` (default), uses `"pos"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not planar (see `is_planar()`), or `scale=` or `center=` is invalid. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~check_planarity`) : The planar embedding this layout draws. [](`~is_planar`) : Whether a graph can be drawn without crossings at all. ## Examples {.doc-examples} `K_4` is planar, so it can be drawn without crossings, with one node inside the triangle of the other three. `refine=False` and `scale=None` keep the grid coordinates: ::: {#a24c576f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=4).layout_planar( refine=False, scale=None, return_dict=True ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: (0.0, 0.0), 2: (4.0, 0.0), 3: (2.0, 1.0), 4: (2.0, 2.0)} ``` ::: ::: ### Flattening an icosahedron The corners and edges of an icosahedron form a planar graph with 12 nodes, 30 edges and 20 triangular faces. `layout_planar()` on the left flattens it with no crossings, one triangle as the outer border and the others nested inside. The spring layout on the right spreads the corners evenly, and many of its edges cross: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#bd02dd89 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} icosa = ec.Graph().add_named_graph("icosahedral") icosa.layout_planar().plot( layout="pos", width=360, height=360, legend=False ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
